# Commands

agentfs takes a command, and the commands that read a workspace take one directory. A first argument that names no command is read as that directory, so the two forms below run the same thing.

```
agentfs <command> [flags] <directory>
agentfs <directory>
```

`agentfs -h`, `agentfs --help` and `agentfs help` print the command list with every flag and every exit code. `agentfs help <command>` prints one command's usage. `agentfs -v` and `agentfs --version` run the version command.

Flags are registered for every command, so `--format` and every setting in [flags.md](flags.md) parse the same way whichever command is invoked. `--format text` is the default. `--format json` writes one `agentfs/report/v1` envelope carrying the schema, the kind, the agentfs version, the workspace root, the exit code and the payload; `--format ndjson` writes the `agentfs/stream/v1` record stream, one record to a line. A command renders the formats named in its own section below and exits `usage` on any other value. The statuses each command exits with are named below too, and described in [exit-codes.md](exit-codes.md).

| Command | Summary | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agentfs watch` | Watch a workspace, drawing it or streaming its changes. | `agentfs watch <directory>` |
| `agentfs scan` | Report the agents a workspace declares, once. | `agentfs scan <directory>` |
| `agentfs validate` | Check every state document against the contract. | `agentfs validate <directory>` |
| `agentfs doctor` | Report how a workspace is observed and what it costs. | `agentfs doctor <directory>` |
| `agentfs schema` | Print the JSON Schema for the state contract. | `agentfs schema` |
| `agentfs version` | Print the build's identity. | `agentfs version` |

## agentfs watch

Watch a workspace, drawing it or streaming its changes.

```
agentfs watch <directory> [flags]
```

Draws the terminal interface: a workspace tree, a file preview and an activity feed, with the run history in place of the tree. The change-detection mode and its counters are on screen, so how the workspace is being read is visible rather than inferred. Key bindings are in [keys.md](keys.md).

Without a terminal on standard output there is nothing to draw, so the command writes the change stream instead — the same output `--format ndjson` asks for on a terminal. It runs until it is interrupted, exiting `interrupted`, or until a write fails. A reader that closes the pipe is recognized on the next record written, so a workspace that goes quiet holds the command open until it is signalled. The record shapes are in [report-envelope.md](report-envelope.md).

Formats: `text`, `ndjson`.

Exits: `0` ok, `2` usage, `3` path, `70` internal, `130` interrupted.

## agentfs scan

Report the agents a workspace declares, once.

```
agentfs scan <directory> [flags]
```

Reads every agent workspace under the root once and prints a line for each: the agent's name, how its state is known, the status it declares, and the task, step, model and problem it declares. A diagnostic about an agent follows that agent's line; a diagnostic about the workspace itself is written to standard error.

Exits `findings` when a document raises an error-severity diagnostic.

Formats: `text`, `json`.

Exits: `0` ok, `1` findings, `2` usage, `3` path, `70` internal.

## agentfs validate

Check every state document against the contract.

```
agentfs validate <directory> [flags]
```

Prints every diagnostic the workspace raises, ordered by document path and then by line, and closes with the number of documents read, the errors, the warnings and the contract version.

Exits `findings` when any diagnostic is an error, so a pipeline gates on the status rather than on the output.

Formats: `text`, `json`.

Exits: `0` ok, `1` findings, `2` usage, `3` path, `70` internal.

## agentfs doctor

Report how a workspace is observed and what it costs.

```
agentfs doctor <directory> [flags]
```

Reports how the workspace is observed: the filesystem under the root and the kind it classifies as, the change-detection mode resolved for that kind, what confinement the platform gives, the agents found, the tracked directories with the sweep budget per cycle, the kernel watch budget, and the contract version.

When the resolved mode sweeps, it also reports the ceiling on filesystem operations per hour this process spends sweeping. Several instances pointed at one shared export cost that figure each.

Formats: `text`, `json`.

Exits: `0` ok, `2` usage, `3` path, `70` internal.

## agentfs schema

Print the JSON Schema for the state contract.

```
agentfs schema [flags]
```

Writes the JSON Schema for the state contract to standard output. It reads no workspace, so an integrator fetches the contract without having one. The members it declares are in [state-schema.md](state-schema.md).

Formats: `text`, `json`.

Exits: `0` ok, `2` usage, `70` internal.

## agentfs version

Print the build's identity.

```
agentfs version [flags]
```

Prints the version, the commit, the build date, the Go version and the contract version.

Formats: `text`, `json`.

Exits: `0` ok, `2` usage, `70` internal.
